sections.overview: The hairy-footed dunnart is an arid-zone marsupial of Australia in the family Dasyuridae.
sections.identification: Fine silvery hairs fringe its broad hind feet, a useful distinction from other dunnarts.
sections.habitat: It uses sandy plains and dunes with open woodland, shrubland or hummock grassland.
sections.diet: In a central Australian field study, ants were an important part of its diet.
sections.behavior: It is nocturnal; its tail stores fat when food is plentiful and can supply energy in lean periods.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted give little detail about its breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: The ant-rich diet reported for this species also links it ecologically with Sminthopsis psammophila; see that profile.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports a global IUCN status of Least Concern.
